title: Batteries Regulation (EU) 2023/1542

productGroups.notes: In force and determinable today even though the passport is future-dated: the Art. 9 mercury and cadmium prohibitions have applied since 2008, carried forward from Directive 2006/66/EC. Scope of the passport obligation is EV, LMT and industrial batteries over 2 kWh. Reg. (EU) 2025/1561 moved the Art. 48(1) due-diligence trigger to 2027-08-18 and the Art. 48(5) Commission guidelines deadline to 2026-07-26. Major obligations remain future-dated: Art. 10(2) minimum performance values from 2027-08-18, Art. 8(1) recycled-content declaration from 2028-08-18, Art. 8(2) minimum shares from 2031-08-18. retentionYears is assumed, not sourced: the Regulation's 10-year figures are documentation retention — technical documentation, EU declaration of conformity, audit reports — not passport availability, which sits with Art. 77 and the unadopted Art. 77(9) implementing act.

notes: The clearest case for separating instrument status from binding status, and passport date from determinability: the act is adopted, its obligations bind now, and its passport is owed from 2027-02-18. retentionYears is assumed, not sourced — the Regulation's 10-year figures are documentation retention (technical documentation, EU declaration of conformity, audit reports), not passport availability, which sits with Art. 77 and the unadopted Art. 77(9) implementing act. Granularity is deliberately unset: the EU registry treats batteries as item-level, but that is the registry's operational position from its user guide, not a level fixed by an adopted act.
